title: A product-preserving derived functor commutes with derived limits

from.place: proof, first step, derived-functor comparison after reconstructing the truncation tower

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be additive, commute with countable products, and admit a right derived functor $RF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For every countable inverse system $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, the derived category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with derived limit $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit], $RF(K)$ is a derived limit of $(RF(K_n))$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$: applying $RF$ to a Roos triangle of $K$ (products taken in $D(\mathcal O_X)$) gives a Roos triangle of $(RF(K_n))$ (products taken in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$), so the canonical comparison $RF(K)\to R\varprojlim_nRF(K_n)$ is an isomorphism.
